Chapter 7. Mentoring the Next Generation.
Over the years, Anna’s role started to change. She wasn’t the outsider anymore, fighting for her place or hoping to be heard. Suddenly, she’d become the mentor—the trusted confidante that others turned to when they needed guidance or just someone to listen. And you know what? She realized her greatest legacy wouldn’t be the policies she helped shape. It would be the people she inspired along the way.
Young women especially came to her, looking for advice on how to navigate a world that still expected them to be quiet, to wait their turn. Anna listened carefully to their stories—their frustrations, their hopes, and everything in between. She remembered what it felt like to be dismissed, to be told her dreams were just too big. So, she encouraged them: Speak up. Trust your instincts. And never let anyone else define your worth.
There was one afternoon that stood out. A young woman came into Anna’s office, hands trembling with nerves. She’d just been offered a job in a field dominated by men—and she was scared she wouldn’t be taken seriously. Anna smiled, thinking back to her own early days. She shared stories of being underestimated, of moments when doubt crept in. But she also talked about learning to trust her own judgment, and letting her work do the talking. The young woman left that day with a new sense of confidence—ready to take on whatever challenges came her way.
Anna’s mentoring didn’t stop with women. She truly believed everyone deserved a chance to be heard, no matter where they came from. She worked with veterans adjusting to civilian life, with immigrants trying to find their footing in a new country, and with young people—men and women—who wanted to make a difference, but didn’t quite know how to start.
She never handed out easy answers. Instead, she asked questions that helped people discover their own path. Anna believed the best leaders are the ones who listen, who keep learning, and who never stop growing.
Over time, Anna’s influence kept spreading. The folks she mentored started becoming leaders themselves, carrying her lessons with them. What they remembered most wasn’t just her wisdom—it was her kindness, her patience, and her unwavering belief in their potential.
Looking back, it’s clear: Anna’s greatest gift was her ability to see the best in others—and to help them see it in themselves.
